prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance toward the right rear corner, pivots on the left foot and swings the right leg forward, reaps the partner's right leg from the outside, and throws uke backwards. Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall).

heading.en: Introductory way of applying the technique

prose.en: Tori's cooperation: Tori pulls up on uke's right sleeve so that uke can take a solid ukemi. Uke's cooperation: Uke puts the right foot forward, receives the o-soto-gari, and takes ushiro-ukemi (rear breakfall) supported on the left foot. Uke takes a stance with the right foot forward, and tori lightly reaps uke's right leg with the right leg and throws. Uke works from a low posture up to a higher one by degrees: half-crouch → standing.

heading.en: Basic way of applying the technique

prose.en: Tori, using a forward tai-sabaki (body movement), breaks uke's balance to the rear and throws by reaping uke's right leg with the right leg. How to take the ukemi: Uke matches tori's o-soto-gari, shifts the body weight onto the left foot, and takes ushiro-ukemi supported on the left foot.
The partners reap each other in turn, practising to maintain balance on the left foot (see-saw).
When uke steps back, apply o-soto-gari out of a large forward tai-sabaki (body movement). When uke comes forward, step with the left foot and apply o-soto-gari.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori must not apply the technique with the hips pulled back. Tori must not apply the technique while the left foot is only shallowly stepped in.
Tori stands firmly and does not fall together with uke. Tori does not reap both of uke's legs.
